svg.text: Figure 17. How the reaction is meant to stop
Four layers, fastest first. The owner phone is not on this list. Glass dump is last-ditch and is not credited until it is tested.
1. Doppler
milliseconds
Fuel gets hotter: U-238 traps widen, more neutrons get caught, fewer left to split.
No moving part. No software. This is the ordinary protection against a sudden rise.
Graphite can go slightly the other way in some layouts. The core must be laid out so that,
from room temperature to 750 C, hotter still means less splitting overall.
2. Drums
seconds
Six B4C drums in the reflector. Springs or gravity drive them IN on overtemp.
Analog. Two channels. Loss of oil pump or Stirling set raises condenser T and trips them.
One drum stuck out: the others still hold the core below a self-sustaining rise.
Leftover splitting-power stays small, so one failure cannot run away on the fast neutrons.
3. Size + earth
hours to days
After drums IN, leftover heat is a space heater, then a heat lamp, then less.
No pump required. 42 t of vault plus soil take < 1 kW. A 1,000 MW plant cannot say this.
A 10-second prompt blip at 35 kW is 350 kJ: a tenth of a kilowatt-hour into a lot of graphite.
There is no 3 GWth inventory to dump. That is the size argument, in numbers.
4. Glass dump
last ditch
Hopper above the core: 80 kg glass frit + 15 kg boron carbide. Plug melts at about 750 C.
Gravity pour. Boron kills reactivity. Glass wets and sets. No power required.
Expected use: once in never. Not credited for normal operation until a furnace test exists.
The fuel and drums are designed so the vault does not get here.
